summary: First 100-mile century, Murphysboro IL to St. Louis MO (101.4 mi, 2,540 ft), started at 7:30am from a Warmshowers host. Tian had crashed on gravel the previous day and rode in the car; the team extended its stay in St. Louis by a day.
slept_at: Nora's home, St. Louis MO (Warmshowers host)
contacts: Jessica (Warmshowers host; start-of-day breakfast, Murphysboro IL area)
Nora and Alex (Warmshowers hosts, St. Louis MO)
planning_notes: Hilly VA/KY ride days (per this post) can have 20-25 climbs over 70-80 mi; Garmin's climb counts are not very intuitive.
Garmin routed a rider straight into a building in a town after Sparta IL; cross-check turn-by-turn with a second map app.
A flatbed passed within about 6 inches of a rider on a highway before St. Louis; the bike trail the route planner suggested into St. Louis kept riders off the highway.
Afternoon thunderstorms were frequent in late June in Missouri; get onto trails and start early to beat them.

summary: Rest day in St. Louis: farmers market at Tower Grove Park, the free St. Louis Zoo, and bike maintenance back at the host's house.
slept_at: Nora's home, St. Louis MO (Warmshowers host)
contacts: Nora and Alex (Warmshowers hosts, St. Louis MO)
planning_notes: Tower Grove Park farmers market is about 1.5 mi walk from the St. Louis host house (team walked).
St. Louis Zoo was free admission (day 24).
Missouri heat and humidity in late June made midday walking exhausting; take breaks in shade.

summary: Long Katy Trail day in light rain from St. Louis to Jefferson City MO (125.1 mi, 3,840 ft as listed); riders went self-supported for about 50 miles before the support car shuttled ahead to cut mileage. The gravel went soft and muddy in the rain.
slept_at: Sarah's home, Jefferson City MO (host; dog Barbara)
contacts: Nora and Alex (St. Louis; arranged the shuttle so the team could cut mileage)
Sarah (host, Jefferson City MO)
planning_notes: Katy Trail (MO): about 260 mi rail-trail, mostly along the Missouri River, fine gravel; the route reaches it around mile 27 from St. Louis.
Katy Trail has occasional bathrooms and benches but no water fountains; ask at restaurants (one restaurant refilled bottles around mile 80).
Rain turns Katy Trail gravel soft and muddy: slower riding and mud up the back.
Shuttle plan: ride self-supported first ~50 mi, then the support car shuttles ahead; riders can then finish the rest of the day on the bike.
Riders drank less in cool rain, but still need water on the trail.

summary: Driving day from Jefferson City to Sedalia MO (69 mi, 3,250 ft): supermarket runs, a minor van accident in a parking lot, a rider-to-rider crash that left Charles and Greta with cuts and bruises, and a church sleepover.
slept_at: Kingdom Life Church, Sedalia MO (church host; pews used as beds)
contacts: Pastor Steve and Anne (Kingdom Life Church, Sedalia MO; Anne shuttled riders and offered laundry)
planning_notes: Kingdom Life Church has no showers: riders showered at Pastor Steve's home and used church laundry. Plan showers in advance.
The church kitchen had no pot lid, so rice cooked to porridge. Bring a lid.
Two riders collided on the route (Charles and Greta): cuts, a sore pinky and a bump. The van's medical kit was used on the spot; keep first aid in the van.
Driving days are heavy: the driver does morning cleanup and dinner planning. Build a shopping list before leaving so you don't need four supermarkets (this driver made four stops).

summary: Chill Katy Trail century from Sedalia MO to Kansas City MO, with the riders playing Mr. White on the trail; two falls happened, Ishaq slipping into the bushes and Charles clipping a metal post and hitting his head.
slept_at: Large Airbnb, Kansas City MO (rented by team)
planning_notes: Katy Trail has metal posts near the path: Charles clipped one at a game stop and was thrown from his bike, hitting his head (briefly dazed); rest stops and game areas should stay clear of posts.
Ishaq slipped off the trail edge into bushes and scraped a knee and elbow.
A rider mounted an iPad to the handlebars with bungees to watch video while riding. It works, but it is a crash and distraction risk; do not copy.

summary: Learning festival at aSTEAM Village, the finale of a 3.5-week STEM camp (intro to machine learning and phases of matter), followed by a sponsor-hosted dinner with Kansas City community leaders.
slept_at: Airbnb, Kansas City MO
learning_festival: aSTEAM Village, Kansas City MO. Finale of a 3.5-week STEM camp where kids built projects over a month. Workshops: intro to machine learning, phases of matter. Team ate lunch with the kids. Sponsor dinner at T'ähä Mexican Kitchen with the aSTEAM coordinator, benefactor, and counselors.
contacts: William Wells (coordinator, aSTEAM Village, KC MO)
Kevin Martinez (benefactor, aSTEAM Village and The Children's Place, KC MO)
Carlos Gomez (president, Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, KC MO)
Juleese (works on reducing incarceration in Kansas City; last name not stated)
planning_notes: Teaching is physically and mentally exhausting for the team; build rest and decompression into the day after a learning festival.
Partnering with a program that has kids for a multi-week project (aSTEAM) let the team go deeper than one-off workshops; worth seeking again.
The post-festival sponsor dinner put the team in touch with local leaders who shared career and volunteering advice; a good way to build local contacts.

summary: Kansas City rest day: a visit to The Children's Place (a trauma treatment center for young children), then a rental-car crisis when the recalled Pacifica's contract could not be renewed, so the team kept the van on an overdue contract. Movie night followed.
slept_at: Airbnb, Kansas City MO
contacts: aSTEAM Village sponsor (unnamed in day 29 post; day 28 names Kevin Martinez as benefactor)
planning_notes: Enterprise rental contracts must be renewed every 30 days. A recall on the 2024 Chrysler Pacifica (side airbag) meant the KC-area branch would not renew, and the metro had no seven-seat vehicles free. Expect rental lead times and plan contract renewals early.
The Children's Place (KC): trauma treatment center for young children; visit was set up by the aSTEAM sponsor. Riders played with kids in small groups; no photos allowed.
When a sponsor dinner was cancelled, the sponsor sent BBQ by DoorDash.

summary: Kansas City MO to Overbrook KS (77.6 mi, 3,363 ft) on July 4th: Ruth rode 2.5 miles in the wrong direction after a reroute, and at a rest stop at a glass-blowing shop, a rider peering into the windows led to a sheriff visit. Ishaq vomited after rationing water and then chugging drinks at a rest stop.
slept_at: Warmshowers host Scott's home, Overbrook KS
contacts: Scott (Warmshowers host, Overbrook KS)
planning_notes: After a road blockage forced a reroute, a bike computer glitch sent Ruth 2.5 mi the wrong way. Confirm direction with a map app before leaving a reroute.
Ishaq rationed water, then chugged 2 Sprites, 2 bottles of water and an apple at rest stop 4 and vomited. Keep water and electrolytes stocked at each stop.
Using a private business as a rest stop: a rider peered into the windows of a glass-blowing shop and the owner readied a gun; a deputy intervened. Ask permission before using a business as a stop.
Scott's Overbrook home had hot tub, pizza and wings, and fireworks in the driveway.

summary: Overbrook KS to Emporia KS (61.9 mi, 1,602 ft) on a Kansas day with about a 20 mph headwind; the team visited Scott's retirement community in the morning, got lost on a closed trail, and then had a second Fourth of July at Didde Catholic Center.
slept_at: Didde Catholic Center, Emporia KS (host Vickie; kitchen, laundry, showers)
contacts: Scott (Overbrook KS host; retirement community visit)
Vickie (host, Didde Catholic Center, Emporia KS)
planning_notes: Kansas plains: riders faced a 20 mph headwind all day on this leg.
A closed trail sent riders onto a windy highway; they could not find the way back to the trail. Check for detours before leaving.
A yellow-taped, do-not-enter bridge was crossed by a rider. It held, but do not cross closed bridges.
Didde Catholic Center (Emporia KS): kitchen, laundry, showers and a basement with ping pong and pool; host gave a key for self-access and allowed fireworks.
Address on the map pointed to private property at one rest stop; the driver had to find another parking spot.

summary: Emporia KS to Newton KS (76.3 mi, 1,602 ft) on US-50: flat, with wide shoulders and no climbs but no shade. Greta snapped a rear derailleur cable and had a nosebleed; the team stayed with hosts Janet and Orvin in Newton.
slept_at: Janet and Orvin's home, Newton KS (Warmshowers hosts; an 1800s house)
contacts: Janet and Orvin (Warmshowers hosts, Newton KS)
planning_notes: US-50 across Kansas: wide paved shoulders, smooth asphalt, no climbs, but no shade, manure smells, and gusts from passing semis.
Greta snapped a rear derailleur cable at the first rest stop (Phillips 66, about 20 mi in). A borrowed bike did not solve it. Carry a spare derailleur cable.
Cedar Point KS rest stop: a near-ghost town with about 3,000 residents across the county; the bank is open by appointment only.
Warmshowers guest book at Janet and Orvin's home is a good read; past riders left notes.

summary: Rest-of-trip learning festival day at Newton Public Library, running Ramona's Caesar cipher workshop with small groups, while Tian and Ishaq went to Wichita KS for gloves and a lost glove was recovered from the highway.
slept_at: Janet and Orvin's home, Newton KS (Warmshowers host)
learning_festival: Newton Public Library, Newton KS. Small groups of kids; Ramona's 'Science of Secrets' workshop on Caesar cipher: discuss ways to share secrets, learn keys, build their own cipher wheels, exchange or crack messages, handout with further reading. Team stayed in the library all day for prep and debugging.
contacts: Janet and Orvin (hosts, Newton KS; took the team to dinner)
planning_notes: Newton Public Library: good LF space with a kids section and computers; small groups worked well.
Science of Secrets (Caesar cipher) workshop: students build their own cipher tools, then exchange messages or try to crack the cipher. Reusable for mixed-age groups.
A glove strapped to the car roof fell off on the highway; recovery took multiple U-turns. Secure gear inside the vehicle or with straps you check before leaving.
Wichita KS had a bike shop and gear store for glove and bike repairs.

summary: Newton KS to Macksville KS (92.6 mi, 1,120 ft) in five legs with frequent rest stops; the route included two miles of loose, slippery dirt with close calls but no falls, and the team stayed at Macksville Christian Church.
slept_at: Macksville Christian Church, Macksville KS (church host; showers and dinner)
contacts: Macksville Christian Church (hosts, Macksville KS)
planning_notes: Newton to Macksville: about 2 miles of very loose, slippery dirt (leg 3). Several close calls, no falls; consider a gravel-averse route.
A shaded rest area in Kansas had signage about wildlife and a bathroom outlet to charge a phone.
Macksville church shower lines: team members rushed ahead to get shower spots.

summary: Driver blog: Macksville KS to Dodge City KS. The team left at 8:10 after a 6:30 wake-up, lost Joseph's glasses (about 30 minutes of searching), and spent the afternoon at a local water park before a host dinner.
slept_at: Host's home, Dodge City KS (host name not stated)
planning_notes: Morning routine: drivers wake riders at 6:30 to leave by 8:00. Six of seven riders left at 8:10 on this day.
Dodge City has a local water park, a good afternoon option when arriving early (about 2pm).
Joseph lost prescription glasses at the morning routine; searching cost about 30 minutes. Keep valuables in one place.

summary: Photo-only post (no narrative) for Dodge City KS to Lakin KS (79.1 mi, 1,436 ft).
slept_at: Church in Lakin KS (rooms provided, per day 37 post; church name not stated)

summary: Lakin KS to Lamar CO (77.25 mi, 1,490 ft): crossed into Mountain Time and Colorado, passed the Amache Internment Camp ruins from a distance, and ended with a church community dinner in Lamar. Joseph also outlined the post-trip van drive from San Francisco to Boston.
slept_at: Lamar Christian Church, Lamar CO (church host; sleep arrangement implied, not explicit)
contacts: Lamar Christian Church (Lamar CO; hosts and Friday community dinner)
planning_notes: Post-trip van return plan: drive the van and gear from San Francisco to Boston rather than buy a one-way rental or ship gear. Route: SF to Seattle, north-central states, national parks, Rust Belt, northern VT/NH; about 10 days.
Colorado's High Plains are wide; the Rockies are not visible for about two days after crossing into Colorado.
Amache Internment Camp ruins are visible from the highway near Granada CO; no close access on this route.
Several riders had persistent finger numbness from the handlebars.

summary: Lamar CO to Fowler CO (86.3 mi, 1,542 ft): Charles's tubeless tire was punctured by a screw and a plug kit burst at 45 PSI, so he rode in the van; the team showered at the pastor's home in Fowler.
slept_at: Church in Fowler CO (church host; showers at Pastor Wayne's home)
contacts: Pastor Wayne (church host, Fowler CO)
planning_notes: Tubeless tire punctured by a screw: the plug kit burst at 45 PSI. Carry a spare tube as a backup for tubeless setups; a tube is an impermanent but stable fix.
Rest stop 3 (a cafe) closed at 3pm; arrive before 3pm.
Pastor Wayne's home (5-minute walk from the Fowler church) had showers; church members served burgers and fresh produce at dinner.

summary: Fowler CO to Colorado Springs CO (99.7 mi, 4,127 ft), a solo day for Tian: a closed trail for bridge construction, a 75 mph I-25 stretch, a closed rest stop, and detours to avoid gravel. Sarah took her first fall on a steep gravel descent.
slept_at: Trinity Lutheran Church, Fowler CO (church host; pew cushions as beds)
contacts: David and Cathie (Greta's grandparents, Colorado Springs; the post spells her name Kathy)
planning_notes: Trail closure for bridge construction near Pueblo: riders can walk through, but the area is chaotic and unsafe for bikes.
I-25 toward Colorado Springs: 75 mph limit; wide shoulder, but exit ramps are dangerous because cars exit at speed.
A planned rest stop (a cafe) was closed; plan on water for 50+ mi with no stops.
Highways near Colorado Springs had no shoulders; some drivers passed very close. Detours to avoid gravel led to these roads.
Steep gravel descent near Colorado Springs: Sarah's first fall of the trip; Greta rode into a bush.

summary: Colorado Springs rest day: Garden of the Gods, a bike-shop tire replacement and Ace Hardware pliers, and a tire re-mount at the hosts' house. Greta's grandmother was briefly hospitalized after a fall, with no broken bones.
slept_at: David and Cathie's home, Colorado Springs CO (hosts)
contacts: David and Cathie (Greta's grandparents, Colorado Springs CO; hosts)
Colorado Springs bike shop (had the needed tire in stock)
planning_notes: Colorado Springs bike shop had the needed tire in stock; a re-mount at a shop was about $25. The team did it themselves with a YouTube video and sealant.
Ace Hardware pliers were $3.50, versus $15 at Home Depot.
Seating a tubeless tire took several tries at about 150 PSI; the tire canister was the tool.
Garden of the Gods is a free park with busy trails and rock formations.

summary: Colorado Springs to Denver CO (66.4 mi, 2,974 ft) on mostly trails (New Santa Fe, Greenland, Plum Creek, Daniels Park). A route road that did not exist sent some riders off-road; a Daniels Park climb and a lake rest stop with a swim were highlights.
slept_at: Maud and Dave's home, Denver CO (MIT alumni hosts)
contacts: Maud and Dave (MIT alumni hosts, Denver CO)
planning_notes: Ride with GPS had a road near mile 33 that does not exist. Some riders went off-road and got lost in a field; verify roads on the map before following a route.
Daniels Park viewpoint: a short, suspicious highway stretch then a category 3 climb; some rain at the top.
Denver: crossing six-lane streets with few gaps is scary; bike paths are otherwise good.
A lake rest stop was among the best of the trip; riders swam there.

summary: Denver learning festival at KIPP Sunshine Peak Academy with rocket launches, followed by an MIT alumni taco dinner in Denver. The team's Enterprise van (Amy) was replaced by an identical silver hybrid.
slept_at: Maud and Dave's home, Denver CO (MIT alumni hosts)
learning_festival: KIPP Sunshine Peak Academy, Denver CO, hosting kids from Boys & Girls Club of Denver. Four groups; rocket launches outdoors (rockets went dozens of feet). One group (ages 5-7) was mostly Spanish-first; a Spanish-speaking teammate (Joseph) partnered with the teacher. Team lunch from Jimmy John's.
contacts: Maud and Dave (MIT alumni hosts, Denver CO; also hosted the alumni event)
KIPP Sunshine Peak Academy (Denver LF host)
Boys & Girls Club of Denver (program whose kids attended)
planning_notes: The rocket launch was the highlight for kids; plan for outdoor launch space and a launch schedule.
For Spanish-first groups, bring a bilingual partner or request a translator from the school; the team had little Spanish.
A table broke during setup in a flood-damaged building; the school moved the team to another room.
Enterprise found a replacement van by phone during the LF; it was the same model in silver hybrid.
Alumni dinner in Denver was organized around the team's stay; a useful way to connect with local MIT alumni.

summary: Denver to Black Hawk CO: Ishaq rode a solo climb of about 18 miles and 4,300 ft into the Rockies, and the team got a new replacement van, Bertha, with a grey 2025 Pacifica hybrid.
slept_at: Amanda's house, near Black Hawk CO (host)
contacts: Amanda (host, near Black Hawk CO)
planning_notes: First mountain climb out of Denver: about 18 mi and 4,300 ft; the final stretch was about 3.5 mph for some riders.
Replacement van Bertha (grey 2025 Pacifica hybrid) started on this day.

summary: Black Hawk CO to Frisco CO (69.75 mi, 7,848 ft): the team crossed Loveland Pass (the trip's highest point), descended the steep dirt Virginia Canyon Road, and finished on the Dillon Reservoir trail after dark.
contacts: Amanda (Black Hawk host; met Sarah halfway in Idaho Springs to swap sunglasses; removed roof storage)
planning_notes: Virginia Canyon Road (Black Hawk to Idaho Springs): about 1,600 ft of steep dirt descent, no guardrail in places (riders called it 'oh my god road'). Wait at the bottom of descents for slower riders.
Loveland Pass: the I-70 tunnel bypasses the pass and bikes are not allowed in it. Summit climb was about 2,000 ft over 10 mi.
Loveland Pass descent: about 2,600 ft over 8.5 mi. Start the pass early; this group finished near 5pm with about 20 mi left.
Dillon Reservoir trail to Frisco is scenic; riders swam in the cold lake.
Roof storage that was not secured thumped loudly on the van during a night drive on I-70; remove it before a long drive.

summary: Frisco CO to Glenwood Springs CO (93.9 mi, 3,266 ft) through Vail Village (cornhole at the rest stop), desert-like terrain, and a Colorado River swim attempt that failed because the current was too fast. Ishaq's birthday cake plan was set up.
slept_at: Barb and Lindsay's home, Glenwood Springs CO (Greta's aunt's house)
contacts: Barb and Lindsay (Greta's aunt's house, Glenwood Springs CO; dog Birdie)
planning_notes: Vail Village rest stop: crowded market with live music and high prices (a $6 banana bread).
Colorado River near Glenwood Springs: current too fast to swim; the team could only stand in the shallows.
A fast cornhole game at the rest stop (the team's only Vail activity) shows that a rest stop can be a longer break if the group is tired.

summary: Learning festival day at Garfield County Public Library in Glenwood Springs, including a machine-learning workshop Tian and Ishaq built over seven festivals. The team also celebrated Ishaq's 22nd birthday and went to the river.
slept_at: Barb and Lindsay's home, Glenwood Springs CO (Greta's relatives; spelled 'Lindsey' in this post)
learning_festival: Garfield County Public Library, Glenwood Springs CO. 7th LF of the trip; teams taught in the same room and rotated groups. Tian and Ishaq's machine-learning workshop for kindergarten to high school: (1) pretend AI classifying images, (2) drawing happy/sad faces to train an online model, (3) unsupervised clustering of drawings, (4) reinforcement-learning maze with a bomb and rewards from -100 to 100.
contacts: Barb and Lindsay (hosts, Glenwood Springs CO)
Garfield County Public Library (LF host; staff fixed a missing takeout order)
planning_notes: The machine-learning workshop has three steps (data, algorithm, decisions) and four activities; it scaled from kindergarten to high school. Good reusable curriculum.
Sharing one room across workshops was noisy but built team camaraderie and let teammates see each other teach.
The library arranged takeout lunch from Kedai Pho & Japanese Cuisine; staff resolved a missing order quickly.

summary: Glenwood Springs CO to Vega State Park CO (56.6 mi, 4,887 ft): a free hot springs stop, a gravel climb between rest stops 2 and 3, and a lakeside campsite where the team cooked grilled cheese and played cards.
slept_at: Vega State Park campground, CO (lakeside campsite)
contacts: Barb and Lindsay (hosts, Glenwood Springs CO; left that morning)
planning_notes: Free hot springs a few miles out of Glenwood Springs; a good first rest stop.
Gravel climb between rest stops 2 and 3: manageable by late July, hard in week one.
Vega State Park: lakeside campsites; shower and facilities are at the far end of the lake, a long way from some sites.
Team grilled-cheese camp dinner: a simple meal that feeds a large group.
